sentences.text:
Petitioner has filed the present writ petition seeking for issuance of writ of certiorari or appropriate writ quashing the order dated 27.01.2023 passed by respondent No.4 in LAQ/ARB/NH- 48/(Haa.Bham)CR.No.67/1/2017-18, LAQ/ARB/ NH- 48/(Haa.Bham)CR.No.8(2)/2018-19 and LAQ/ARB/NH- 48/(Haa.Bham)CR.No.23/2020-21 as per Annexure-F confirming the award passed by respondent No.3 in No.LAQ/SLAO/HSN/AWD/HSN-6/MALALI/2015-16 dated 30.11.2015,

N o . L A Q / S L A O / H S N / A W D / H S N - 1 1 / M A L A L I / 2 0 1 6 - 1 7 d a t e d 2 9 . 0 8 . 2 0 1 7 ,
No.LAQ/SLAO/HSN/AWD/HSN- 6A/MALALI/2015-16 dated 29.11.2017 & No. LAQ/SLAO/HSN/
Missing.AWD/HSN-20/MALALI/2019-20 dated 10.06.2020 as per Annexures-A, A1, A2, A3 and A4 respectively.
Petitioner contends that the award was passed on 30.11.2015 as regards the acquisition of the petitioner's lands bearing Sy. Nos. 381, 382/4, 384/1, 387/3 and 387/4.

Aggrieved by the value fixed, petitioner has filed application under Section 64 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, before the Deputy Commissioner, Hassan.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The Deputy Commissioner and Arbitrator, Hassan, dismissed the application by order under Section 3-G(5) of the National Highways Act, 1956.
The said facts are not in dispute.

3. Grievance against the award of the Arbitrator under Section 3-G(5) of the National Highways Act,
1956, is a matter that can be assailed only by the statutory remedy under Section 34 of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act.

Though vehement submissions have been made to waive off the alternative remedy, however, in light of the substantive statutory remedy available, it would not be appropriate for this Court to intervene and NC: 2023:KHC:21224 interfere with the hierarchy of statutory redressal mechanism.
4. Accordingly, the petition is disposed off without adjudication.
The petitioner is at liberty to challenge the award of the Deputy Commissioner at Annexure-F by taking recourse to the provisions of Arbitration and Conciliation Act, if so advised.
The time spent before this Court to be excluded while calculating the period of limitation in the event such circumstances arise.
All contentions are kept open.
The certified copies/original documents to be returned to the petitioner.
Accordingly, petition is disposed off.
